name: PT Dian Swastatika Sentosa Tbk

frontmatter.title: DSSA: the parts, the upstream and the premium
frontmatter.summary: DSSA is a Sinar Mas conglomerate whose coal arm sits in a separately listed subsidiary. The parts are worth Rp233; the price is 3.6x that value. The konglo lens keeps only part of the premium over twelve months, giving a target of Rp518 and a SELL. The subsidiary's dividends reach the parent; the parent hoards them.
thesis: The parts — the listed coal stake at the covered subsidiary's house target, the non-coal segments at audited net book, the unallocated remainder, net of non-controlling interests and less a holding-company discount — are worth Rp233 after twelve months, far below the Rp750 price.
The own-history P/E and P/BV are dropped, not down-weighted: they are struck on the price history OJK found manipulated and sit several times above the parts.

The upstream is real: the parent receives its controlling share of the coal subsidiary's distributions. What never happens is a distribution from DSSA to its own shareholders, so the discount is a hoarding discount, not a dead channel.
Power and technology are fallback book marks, not house-card valuations; the report tests them and shows what a book haircut is worth.
PT SMT, which we infer is the controlling shareholder, has been fined over manipulation of trading in DSSA's own shares; the konglo lens slows the premium's compression rather than removing it.

catalysts.event: OJK hands the sanction letters over in person to PT SMT (inferred to be the controlling shareholder) and to nine exchange members
The regulator describes its market-conduct sanctions as the largest in its history and keeps criminal escalation open
IDX minimum free-float step takes effect for large caps; DSSA's free float clears the raised minimum but the group remains in the HSC regime
MSCI consultation on moving Indonesia to Standalone status closes, with a decision due by 30 June 2027

blocks.text: **This revision removes the OJK-tainted multiples and corrects the upstream claim; the house maintains SELL and the Rp518 target.** The lift from the prior published (third-version) level to this target was approved with the fourth version, not made in this update. The fundamental now rests entirely on the parts: the coal stake at the covered subsidiary's house target, the non-coal businesses at audited segment net book, plus the unallocated corporate remainder, net of the non-controlling interests that belong to outside holders and less a holding-company discount. That is Rp233 a share after twelve months, or Rp207 today [S0]. The price is Rp750, or 3.6x fundamental value [S0]. The konglo lens keeps part of that premium because a float of 21.5% and a locked controlling-plus-treasury block set the marginal price: the base regime case closes 45% of the log gap for Rp472, and probability-weighted across the three regime scenarios the target is Rp518, a -31.0% total return [S0]. The rating is SELL.

**Three corrections.** First, the own-history P/E and P/BV are dropped, not cut to a token weight: they are struck on the tape the regulator found was planned, structured and price-lifted [S10, S13, S14], and because they sat several times above the parts, even a ten per cent weight supplied about half the old fundamental. Second, the parent has received subsidiary dividends: the cash flow records the outside shareholders' share at USD 105m in FY2025 and USD 237m in FY2024 [S9], and the subsidiary's note records a total FY2024 distribution of USD 500m to all shareholders [S9]; at the 51.0% stake, the controlling share reaches DSSA and is reinvested. Third, the card's holdco deductions are applied: overhead capitalised at ten times the sourced office line, and a tested parent net-debt position [S9, F62].

**The variant view.** The market is not paying for the coal arm, which sits in a separately listed subsidiary valued at a fraction of the parent, nor for the non-coal parts at audited book. It is paying a 3.6x premium to the whole. The konglo lens explains why that premium can persist — thin float, index deletions and a live sanction — but it does not make the premium value. We mark the subsidiary at its house target, below its own quote, so the parts are not flattered by the market's optimism about the child [S0]. The nearest bull catalyst is not a first upstream from the subsidiary, which already happens, but a first distribution from DSSA to its own shareholders.

DSSA reports in US dollars and describes itself as an energy and infrastructure company [S9]. Revenue comes from four segments — captive steam and electricity, fertilizer and chemicals trading, coal mining and trading, and cable television, internet and technology, plus small renewable and other lines [S9].

Coal dominates: mining and trading revenue was 2,488 USD m against group revenue of 2,791.2 [S9, S0], behind the company's statement that mining is about nine-tenths of revenue [S3]. The coal business sits in PT Golden Energy Mines Tbk, listed since 2011, in which DSSA holds 51.0% directly [S9, S3]. The mines operate under coal contracts of work (CCoW), whose royalty and permit terms the group flags as a margin risk [S9]. The minority interest of 444.4 is largely the coal subsidiary's outside owners [S9].

The other pillars are smaller. Technology revenue was 212 USD m last year and 170 USD m in the first half, roughly double the prior period [S9, S6]; fertilizer and chemicals was 90.9 USD m; power has no external revenue because the fee is earned inside the group [S9]. The group says the energy pillar funds the build-out of the others, its stated reason for not paying a dividend [S6, S9].

Ownership is concentrated: PT Sinar Mas Tunggal holds 59.9%, insider holdings are 66.3% and the free float is 21.5% [S9, S0]. The entity the regulator has just sanctioned is named in the sources only as PT SMT [S10, S14]; we infer it is the controlling shareholder PT Sinar Mas Tunggal, an inference no source confirms. Market capitalisation is 116,049,092,437,500.0 with about 427,113,583,150.8 traded a day, so no liquidity discount applies [S0]; the fifty-two week range of 432.0 to 4,640.0 shows the repricing [S0].

A listed parent that owns stakes in separately listed children usually trades at a discount to what
those stakes are worth: minority holders cannot direct the cash, cannot force a distribution, and bear
the cost of whatever the parent builds next. The discount narrows only when something specific and
dated forces value up to the parent.

DSSA is five businesses, and the house card says mark each on its own terms rather than apply a blanket multiple to the group [S9]. The largest is thermal coal. The coal price reaches DSSA through the listed subsidiary's own quote and house target, not through a mine model we build here, so the coal path enters the parts as the market's and the subsidiary's own view rather than a second, independent forecast [S9, S12].

Power is a captive processing fee with a large asset base and no external revenue [S9]. Chemicals is a low-margin distribution book [S9]. Digital infrastructure — broadband, homepasses and a data-centre build — is the fastest-growing revenue line [S6, S9]. Competitively, the group is a follower: the coal producer is mid-curve with a wide calorific range and a domestic, China and India customer mix [S9]; broadband and data centres face far larger incumbents in a scale business with front-loaded capital [S6, S9]; chemicals is a price-taker [S9]. Only the power processing agreement has a semblance of a moat, and it is the part with the largest book and the least external revenue [S9].

Two external influences matter: the market-conduct file against the controlling shareholder, which the house framework reads as a manipulation-class flag [S10, S14], and the coal royalty and permit regime, which the group flags as a margin risk [S9] and which reaches our target through the subsidiary's model.

Revenue fell to 2,791.2 last year from 3,017.8, and gross margin compressed to 33.7% from 40.7% [S0]. Net profit to the parent was 230.5, of which minorities took 130.7 [S0, S9], and return on equity was 16.0% [S9].

The data pack's depreciation is a fraction of the real charge because the cash-flow statement uses the direct method and carries no add-back; the segment note discloses consolidated D&A of 78.2 USD m and 83.6 USD m for the last two years, and the model carries that restated charge [S9]. Two splits make older per-share metrics not like-for-like [S0].

The forecast reproduces the last audited year's economics. Revenue growth of 10.0% takes the top line to 3,070.3, on the two plan numbers the company has disclosed: first-half technology revenue roughly doubled [S6, F20], and the coal subsidiary guides 58 Mt of sales against the 55.0 Mt it itself reports for 2025 [S12, F48, F79], about five and a half per cent higher, while DSSA's consolidated coal sales were 56.7 Mt [S9, F1]. Gross margin of 33.7% and EBITDA margin of 17.2% are held at last year's levels because no source supports a squeeze or a recovery [S0, S9], giving EBITDA of 527.0 and net profit to the parent of 164.3 [S0]. **Reconciling the first half.** The first half ran at roughly a third higher group revenue, with coal up nearly thirty per cent and technology up nearly ninety per cent [S6]; we do not extrapolate that run-rate because it is struck against a weak prior-year half and a coal-price run-rate the company's own volume plan does not repeat. The full-year forecast instead applies the subsidiary's own volume plan (about five and a half per cent higher, above) and holds margins at last year's level; that combination is the most likely path, not a cautious one, and it is why FY2026E growth sits below the first-half actual. Beyond FY2026E the revenue path is a hand-set fade that feeds only the zero-weighted earnings cross-checks and does not reach the target, which is the sum of the parts [S0, S9].

Capex of 513.7 against EBITDA of 527.0 leaves free cash flow to the firm of 38.6, and the same comparison was negative last year at -99.4 [S0]: spending absorbs essentially all the businesses generate, concentrated in the non-coal pillars [S9, S6]. We hold capex at last year's ratio without a source to change it [S0, S9].

The balance sheet carries cash of 575.5, debt of 1,486.2 and minorities of 444.4, for net debt of 910.6 and net debt to EBITDA of 1.9 [S0]. This is not charged twice: each part is valued after its own liabilities [S9]. The parent's bonds are inside the segment marks — segment liabilities of 2,121 USD m are within two per cent of consolidated liabilities (assets of 4,415 USD m less equity of 2,261 USD m) — so netting them again would double-count [S9]. The guarantees are a contingent claim in section six [S9].

**Earnings quality.** Accruals are negative in two of the last three years and marginally positive in the third: operating cash was 330 USD m, 693 USD m and 1,031 USD m against net profit of 361.2, 542.8 and 865.3 [S0, S9]. Cash covered profit in two of the three years and fell short by a whisker in the third, well inside the threshold. Free cash flow to the firm turns negative — -99.4, -139.4, 307.6 [S0] — a capital-spending story, not an accruals one. Technology assets grew from 1,162 USD m to 2,208 USD m in a year [S9]. The regulatory action is not a listing-status action on the issuer [S10, S14]. One sanctioned member is PT SS, whose director received an underwriter-licence freeze [S14, F57]; no DSSA entity or director is among the sanctioned parties [S14].

Related-party purchases were 0.4% of cost of revenues and the related-party slice of G&A was 0.9%, mainly family property, telecom and insurance entities [S9]. The larger exposure is structural: allocating a data centre or broadband network between listed and unlisted vehicles is the family's choice [S9, S6], and the data-centre build already runs through a related party — KMG bought the package for the group's data-centre project from PT LG Sinarmas Technology Solutions for Rp1.2tn [S9, F67].

**PSAK 16.** The power book does not carry a revaluation surplus today: the plants were sold in 2024, the decrease in the surplus was 160 USD m, the cumulative increment transferred to retained earnings was USD 111m, and the surplus line is nil [S9]. **Structure flags**: two splits, the restructuring that moved the subsidiary stake onto the parent's books, the elimination column of -1,954 USD m, and the treasury block of 1,516 million shares, 19.7% of issued capital [S9]. The disclosure items are optics-class; the regulator's finding that trading in DSSA's shares was planned, structured and price-lifting is manipulation-class, and it sits at the controlling shareholder rather than in the issuer's accounts [S10, S13, S14].

The house card values a holding company on its parts, less holdco net debt and a discount the base rate says persists [S0]. The parts carry 100% of the blend: the own-history P/E and P/BV are dropped because both sat several times above the parts and are struck on the tape OJK found manipulated [S0, S10, S13, S14]. The cost of equity is 12.4% and the weighted average cost of capital 10.8%, built in the table [S0].

**The parts.** Each mark is a listed price or an audited segment book; the bridge reconciles to consolidated equity and then cuts the consolidated total back to the parent's share. The coal stake is at the covered subsidiary's house target, not its quote, because the konglo card marks a covered listed subsidiary at its house target and that target sits below the market price. The house target and the quote come from GEMS.JK's own covered report and model, the subsidiary rated HOLD with its house target below its quote [S20].

| Part | Mark | | --- | --- | | PT Golden Energy Mines Tbk, 51.0% stake | house target [S20] | | Steam and electricity | net book, fallback [S9] | | Cable TV, internet and technology | net book, fallback [S9] | | Fertilizer and chemicals | net book [S9] | | Renewable energy | net book [S9] | | Other | net book [S9] | | Intra-group elimination | deduction [S9] | | Unallocated corporate and tax remainder | value [S9] | | Non-controlling interests | deduction [S9] |

Marks are assets less liabilities: 2,659 USD m less 668 USD m, 2,208 USD m less 1,114 USD m, 57.4 USD m less 32.6 USD m, 75.2 USD m less 1.0 USD m, 37.6 USD m less 0.6 USD m, the elimination -1,954 USD m less -197 USD m, and the remainder equity 2,261 USD m less segment net assets [S9].

**Power and technology are fallbacks, and tested.** Power has no external revenue and no segment result; its FY2024 comparative result was -0.2 [S9], so a fee business with no disclosed profit is at net book rather than an invented multiple. Technology has a segment result of 142 USD m, before operating expense; against net book of 2,208 USD m less 1,114 USD m that is about an eighth of book, and after the FY2024 comparative operating expense of USD 78.6m it is a mid-single-digit return, which does not prove the book [S9]. We keep net book at par as the most likely mark, not as caution: no house card exists for these unlisted segments, audited segment net book is the only disclosed measure of their capital, and the technology result shows a positive, if thin, return on it. A ten per cent haircut is the bear's mark and a re-rating on a future segment-return disclosure is the bull's; the book is a floor with a range [S0, S9]. The PSAK 16 objection is answered: the plants were sold, the cumulative increment was transferred to retained earnings, and the surplus line is nil [S9, F49, F76].

**The reconciliation.** The segment books are stated in full, so the parts must be cut back to the parent's share. Consolidated equity is 2,261 USD m [S9], of which total non-controlling interests are 444 USD m [S9] and the coal subsidiary 350 USD m [S9]. The coal segment's net book — 1,051 USD m less 502 USD m — is replaced by the parent's 51.0% share of the GEMS house target; because GEMS's own net assets (implied by the 350 USD m NCI at the minority share) exceed that segment book, the deduction is the total NCI less the coal book the GEMS mark already removes beyond the parent's share. The bridge is equity less that deduction plus the GEMS mark over the coal net book [S9]; the elimination is already inside consolidated equity, so there is no second elimination, and the remainder is positive [S9].

**Why audited book, not the first-half equity.** The SOTP starts from the audited FY2025 segment books, not the higher first-half-2026 consolidated equity [S6]. The segment marks are audited and the half-year uplift sits largely in the coal column, which the GEMS house mark already replaces at the subsidiary's own value; reading the increase straight into the parent's equity would count that uplift twice. The choice is disclosed, and it is why the valuation does not rise with the first-half equity.

**The holdco bridge.** The parent's bonds and sukuk are inside segment liabilities — segment liabilities of 2,121 USD m are within two per cent of consolidated liabilities, and the Phase IV issue alone was Rp0.3tn of bonds plus Rp1.2tn of sukuk [S9, F68, F69] — so netting them again would double-count. What is not in the marks is parent overhead: the parent-level office expense of USD 3.9m [S9, F62], capitalised at ten times, is the deduction, a floor because the parent-only share of salaries is not published. The guarantees are a contingent claim in section six [S9, F63-F66].

**The upstream, corrected.** The old report said the parent had never received a dividend; that was wrong. The cash flow records NCI dividends of USD 105m in FY2025 and USD 237m in FY2024 [S9], and the subsidiary's note records total distributions of USD 500m for FY2024 and USD 500m for FY2023 to all holders [S9]. At 51.0% the parent receives the controlling share; it covers the capitalised office cost about six and a half times on FY2024 and almost three times on FY2025 [S9, F58-F62]. The discount is a hoarding discount — cash arrives and is not passed on — not a dead channel.

**The discount.** A discount of twenty to forty per cent persists indefinitely, and a narrower discount needs a dated catalyst that upstreams cash [S0]. The one precedent is stale: a 2023 buyback took 484 USD m of stock off the market, of which 1,516 million shares, 19.7% of issued capital, still sits in treasury; part was reissued in 2024 for 48.9 USD m [S9]. The policy permits up to 30.0% of net profit and the parent has never paid a dividend [S9, S0]. We charge 30%, the middle of the persistent band, on the base rate and the non-enforcement structure — the related-party flow, the treasury overhang and the cross-guarantees [S9, F46-F67]; the stale buyback argues against the wide end, that structure against the tight end. The OJK trading sanction is not a second discount: the konglo card assigns it to the lens, and it is counted there once [S10, S14]. Even the tight end leaves the parts below the price [S0].

The sum of the parts is Rp207 a share; grown at the cost of equity for a year, with no dividend leg, that is the fundamental value of Rp233 [S0]. The price is Rp750, so the gap is the premium ratio of 3.6x, not the final target's expected return; the -31.0% figure is the return to the lens target only [S0].

**The konglo lens.** The engine measures the log premium of 1.3 [S0] and assumes only a share closes in twelve months because the marginal price is set by float: 21.5% of the capital trades [S9, S0]. The closing share is slowed by HSC listing, exit from the IHSG and the index family, and the live sanction [S15, S16, S10, S14], and is run over three regime scenarios, weighted (base at 50%): **bear** closes 85% of the gap for Rp282; **base** closes 45% for Rp472; **bull** closes none and the premium holds for Rp843 [S0]. Probability-weighted, the target is Rp518. We do not shade the parts toward or away from the market price [S0].

The grid is driven by the discount and the cost of equity and reports pre-lens values; it does not bracket the target because the lens adds most of the distance to the price [S0]. Section five shows the subsidiary's bear target effect instead.

On this method the target is set by the marked parts and the discount; the largest part is the subsidiary's house value, imported from its own model, so the grid shocks the discount and the two scenarios are discount scenarios in form [S0]. **Bear**: the governance file escalates, nothing is returned to DSSA holders, the coal marker normalises and the digital build consumes capital. The subsidiary already publishes a bear target; at that target the controlling stake is worth less than half its base mark, and the parent's fundamental value falls by about a quarter, while the lens cushions the twelve-month target [S0]. A ten per cent haircut to the two fallback book marks has a similar order of effect. Two structure tails sit outside every mark. First, the cross-guarantee stack: DSSA guarantees EMR facilities of Rp3.6tn, Rp0.4tn and Rp2.0tn and the PT SMPlus data-centre facility of Rp0.4tn [S9, F63-F66] — a call on the full stack is about a seventh of the gross parts and would wipe out the capitalised parent overhead many times over, so it is sized as a bear tail, not netted in the base. Second, dilution: the annual report's funding waterfall runs internal cash, then short-term debt, then long-term debt, then new shares [S9]; we found no announced rights issue or placement in the sources reviewed, a checked absence rather than proof [S9]. A discounted placement against a controlled price is the classic per-share leak in this structure. **Bull**: a dated capital-allocation signal — a repeat buyback, a first distribution to DSSA holders or a stake sale — narrows the discount, with the 58Mt plan delivered and technology already doubling [S6, S9, S12]: a value of Rp237 and a target of Rp266, with base at 50% [S0]. Even at the subsidiary's own bull target the parent's lens target stays below the price: the largest component is a covered subsidiary's house target the parent does not control [S9].

**The konglo regime scenarios.** The lens reads the price at 3.6x fundamental value and asks how much of the 1.3 log gap the regime lets close [S0]. DSSA is on the HSC list and out of the IHSG from 2 November 2026 [S15, S16]; it was deleted from the MSCI Global Standard and FTSE Large Cap indexes in 2026 [S17, S18]; and the controlling shareholder carries an OJK sanction with criminal escalation open [S10, S13, S14]. The free float of 21.5% clears the raised fifteen per cent minimum, so no forced supply step sits in the window [S0, S19]. The dated catalysts are the MSCI Standalone consultation, feedback closing on 30 April 2027 with a decision by 30 June 2027 [S6], the IDX free-float deadlines from 31 March 2027 [S19], and the enforcement file [S13]. The bear case is that the premium the lens keeps is what the 2026 regime is dismantling, so a faster unravel is a real risk.

Five risks carry weight. **Governance (high likelihood, high impact)**: the controlling shareholder has been fined over manipulation of DSSA's shares, exchange members were sanctioned, and criminal escalation stays open [S14, S10, S13]; we read it as a regime factor the konglo lens carries [S0]. **Capital allocation (high likelihood, high impact)**: capex absorbs essentially all of group EBITDA, the parent receives the subsidiary's distributions but passes none to its shareholders, and the equity has no yield support [S0, S9]. **Coal-market (medium likelihood, medium impact)**: the coal stake is marked at the subsidiary's house target, so a lower coal marker lowers the largest part directly [S9]. **Disclosure (high likelihood, medium impact)**: no segmental operating profit is published for the largest book-value segments; a technology-profit disclosure would be the biggest positive change [S9]. **Currency (medium likelihood, medium impact)**: the group reports in dollars, so the rupiah value of the parts moves with the exchange rate while the businesses do not [S0].
A dated action that distributes cash to DSSA's own shareholders — a dividend, buyback or stake sale — would justify a narrower discount [S9], while a criminal escalation widens it [S13, S10].

**The konglo profile.** DSSA is the Sinar Mas group's energy and infrastructure holding, the Widjaja family's listed vehicle and the parent of the separately listed coal miner [S9]. The controlling holding company holds 59.9% and insider holdings are 66.3%, leaving a free float of 21.5% [S9, S0]. That float clears the raised fifteen per cent minimum [S0, S19], but DSSA is on the HSC list and out of the IHSG from 2 November 2026 [S15, S16], and was deleted from the MSCI Global Standard and FTSE Large Cap indexes in 2026 [S17, S18]. The live enforcement item is the OJK manipulation sanction against PT SMT (inferred to be the controlling shareholder), the largest in the regulator's history and open to criminal escalation [S10, S13, S14]. The marginal price is set by a few per cent of the capital [S0].

**Structure flags.** Cross-guarantees: DSSA guarantees EMR facilities of Rp3.6tn, Rp0.4tn and Rp2.0tn and the PT SMPlus data-centre facility of Rp0.4tn [S9, F63-F66], contingent claims disclosed and not netted in the parts. Treasury: the 2023 buyback left 1,516 million shares, or 19.7% of issued capital, in treasury [S9, F46, F47] — potential supply and a governance overhang. Pledges: the report discloses pledges of GEMS-group shares and receivables for the subsidiary's bank facilities [S9, F74]; we found no disclosure of a pledge of the controlling shareholder's DSSA stake, a checked absence, not proof. Dilution: the stated funding waterfall runs internal cash, then short-term debt, then long-term debt, then new shares [S9]; no rights issue or placement is announced in the sources reviewed, but the channel is live [S9]. Related-party assets: the data-centre build runs through PT LG Sinarmas Technology Solutions at Rp1.2tn [S9, F67], and allocating assets between listed and unlisted vehicles is the family's choice [S9]. Each widens the warranted discount.

**Ownership and the sanction.** Minority holders have no practical influence over board composition or the decision to reinvest [S9]. The authority imposed an administrative fine of 1.5 Rp trn on the PT SMT (inferred to be the controlling shareholder) over manipulation of DSSA's shares, found the manipulation planned and structured and price-lifting, sanctioned 9 exchange members and warned eight sales staff, and handed the letters over on 21 October [S10, S14]. It will escalate to a criminal investigation if the evidence supports one and calls the sanction the largest in its history [S13]. On the house framework this is a manipulation-class flag; the konglo card routes it to the regime lens, so it slows the premium's compression there and is not counted a second time in the holdco discount [S10, S11, S13, S14].

**Dividend and ESG.** The policy permits up to 30.0% of net profit [S9] and the parent has paid none to its own shareholders, on the company's stated explanation that its subsidiaries require the capital [S9]. The subsidiary does pay: the cash flow and its dividend note show distributions to all shareholders, of which the parent receives the controlling share [S9, F58-F61]. An upstream that arrives at the parent and stops there is the whole cost of the structure — a hoarding discount — and it is why the dividend-yield method is dropped [S0, S9]. On ESG the exposures are the ordinary ones for Indonesian thermal coal at the subsidiary, plus the governance sanction, on which this name would not pass a controlling-shareholder conduct screen today [S10], and a transition claim resting on disclosure too thin to underwrite [S9, S6].

Only the regulatory file and the index calendar carry dates. The sanction letters were handed over on 21 October to PT SMT (inferred to be the controlling shareholder) and exchange members [S14, S13]; whether the issuer faces action and whether the investigation reaches the courts is what sets the governance discount [S10, S11]. The HSC names leave the IHSG calculation from 2 November 2026 [S16], the IDX free-float step lands on 31 March 2027 [S19], and the MSCI Standalone consultation closes on 30 April 2027 with a decision by 30 June 2027 [S6]. The rest are undated watch items [S9].

The monitorables are method-specific. Any distribution from DSSA to its own shareholders — a dividend, buyback or stake sale — would attack the discount directly; the subsidiary's upstream already reaches the parent, so the missing leg is the parent's payout [S9]. Segmental operating profit and capital employed for technology, power and chemicals would let us mark those parts on their own cards instead of at fallback book [S9]. And who pays for the data centre and broadband build, at what return, is the item that would most change the parts valuation [S6, S9].

bear.narrative: The discount widens to the wide end of the persistent band: the governance file escalates to a criminal investigation, the group returns nothing upstream again, and the coal subsidiary's own quote carries the coal risk while the digital build keeps consuming capital. The subsidiary is itself a covered konglo name: its house target already blends its own bear, base and bull scenarios, and at its published bear target the 51% stake is worth less than half its base mark. The engine's SOTP mark is the subsidiary's probability-weighted house target, not a live coal model, so the scenario lever here is the discount; the report shows the coal-stake bear mark separately rather than pretending the engine re-prices GEMS.

bull.narrative: The discount narrows to the tight end of the persistent band on a capital-allocation signal we can see coming — a repeat of the 2023 holdco buyback, a first dividend, or a stake sale crystallising a mark [S9, F44] — with the coal subsidiary's 58Mt plan delivered [S12] and the digital pillar growing into its invested capital because technology revenue already roughly doubled in the first half [S6, F20], so the coal mark holds up and the discount narrows. Even here the parts do not reach the market's price.

enforcement.note: planned, structured trading manipulation of DSSA shares in 2023-2026 that pushed the price up; PT SMT fined Rp1.5tn, brokers fined and sales staff warned

konglo.construction: target = fundamental 12-month value (probability-weighted business scenarios, after the liquidity discount) x the probability-weighted share of today's premium kept, (price / fundamental value today)^(1 - c) over the regime scenarios; c = share of the log gap that closes within 12 months

assumptions.label: Revenue growth
assumptions.basis: FY2026E is anchored on the two plan numbers that ARE traceable and the last actual. The company's own target table carries revenue targets for FY2025 and FY2024 and gives no 2026 revenue number at all [S9, F15]. What the register DOES give for 2026 is the listed coal subsidiary's own plan — 58Mt of production and sales, above the 54.95Mt the subsidiary itself reports for 2025 [S12, F48, F79] — and the group's first-half technology revenue, roughly doubled year on year to USD 170.49m [S6, F20]. Coal is roughly nine-tenths of group revenue [S9, F7]. A full-year doubling of the USD 211.8m technology line [S9, F38] adds about eight per cent to the group, and the coal volume plan adds about five and a half, which puts FY2026E about a tenth above FY2025A. That is a drift UP from the last actual that rests only on the two sourced plan numbers, not on a coal-price assumption. From FY2027E the first-half technology step is not extrapolated a second time and no source supports volume beyond the 2026 plan, so the top line fades toward the last actual rather than compounding; the fade feeds only the small earnings cross-checks and does not set the target, which is the sum of the parts.

assumptions.label: Gross margin at base input costs
assumptions.basis: Set at the last audited year's own gross margin (consolidated gross profit over revenue, FY2025A [S0, S9]) rather than the three-year average the starter carried, because the most-likely rule is that FY+1 reproduces the last actual year's economics and no source supports a further squeeze. The three-year average is flattered by FY2023, when the coal marker was roughly a third higher than it is today, so carrying it forward would import a peak-year margin into the forecast.

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: The last audited year's own ratio of SG&A and other operating expense to revenue [S0], held flat in real terms. The group's overhead carries the technology, chemicals and corporate functions as well as the mine, and nothing in the LK sources a step down; a decline would be an unsourced haircut.

assumptions.label: D&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: Set from the LK's OWN depreciation and amortisation, not the data pack's cash-flow feed: the group reports consolidated D&A of USD 78.2m for FY2025 and USD 83.6m for FY2024 in the segment note [F17, F18], roughly three times the pack's direct-method figure, and the ratio of that restated charge to revenue is what the forecast carries. The pack's D&A is small because the IDX cash-flow statement is prepared on the direct method and carries no add-back.

assumptions.label: Capex / revenue
assumptions.basis: The last audited year's own ratio of capital spending to revenue [S0, S9], held flat. The group spends across the mine, the power assets, the broadband network and the data-centre build, and that spending absorbed essentially all of group EBITDA in the recent audited years; the ratio is the witnessed rate, not a target, and no source supports cutting it.

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(nwc, revenue))

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(tax, pbt))

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(interest_expense, debt[-1]))

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(interest_income, cash[-1]))

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: Held at the engine default (no new borrowing) with the caveat stated in the report rather than a fabricated financing plan: the LK says only that long-term bank borrowings may rise in the next few years to fund new projects and that the group funds capex from internal cash first, then short-term debt, then long-term debt, then new shares [S9], which is not a number we can date. On this method the forecast balance sheet feeds only the small earnings and book cross-checks, not the target, so an unsourced debt schedule would add false precision. Where the modelled cash path runs thin past the forecast horizon the report says so plainly [S9].

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(minority, np))

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: Zero, and sourced rather than assumed by omission: the group's policy permits a distribution of up to 30% of net profit [F14], but the accounts record no dividend payment in any reported year [S0, S9] and the company states it has not distributed dividends because its subsidiaries require substantial capital expenditure [S9]. A payout we cannot source, on a name that has never paid one, would be a fabricated leg in the blend; the engine therefore drops the yield method entirely.

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: The primary method is a sum of the parts with a holding-company discount, so no perpetual growth rate reaches the target; this input only frames the cross-checks. It is set at the house's long-run USD inflation assumption, below the house cap for a USD-reporting name, because a coal-heavy conglomerate should not be assigned perpetual real growth.

assumptions.label: Holding-company discount to SOTP
assumptions.basis: Anchored on the house holdco archetype, not on a hope of narrowing: the base rate for holdco and SOTP names is that a discount of 20-40% persists indefinitely, and the recorded case file requires a NAMED, DATED catalyst that actually upstreams cash before a narrower discount can be underwritten. We hold 30%, the middle of that band. The stale end of the evidence argues against the wide end: this name has ONE capital-return precedent on the record — a holdco buyback of 154,105,327 shares in August-September 2023 for USD 483.8m, part of which was reissued to a third party in August 2024 [S9, F44, F45] — but it is three years old, has never been repeated, and the parent has never paid a dividend to its own holders [S0, S9]. The governance file argues against the tight end on its own merits and is NOT the OJK trading sanction: related-party purchases of family property, telecom and insurance, the data-centre package bought from a family affiliate, the treasury overhang and the cross-guarantees [S9, F46-F67] are the discount-widening structure. The OJK manipulation finding is assigned once, to the konglo lens (enforcement_manipulation), per the konglo card, and is not counted again here. The choice within the band is not load-bearing: the parts value is so far below the price that even the tight end leaves the bull leg below the market price.

challenges.challenge: The summary says "the house maintains SELL and lifts the target from the prior published level to Rp518." The prior published v4 (dashboard meta: rating SELL, tp Rp518, published 2026-10-28; history: v3 Rp387) already carried Rp518, and this update's model is byte-identical to history/v4 (same tp_final 517.586, rating SELL), so the target is maintained, not lifted. A reader comparing with the published record sees a false track-record claim.
challenges.answer: Summary now reads 'maintains SELL and the {{val.tp_final|px}} target'; the lift from the prior published third-version level is stated as history approved with the fourth version, not this update. Rating and target unchanged.

challenges.challenge: Section 3 (and assumptions.revenue_growth) says "the coal subsidiary guides 58Mt of sales against the 56.7 Mt it sold in 2025 [S12, F48]." The cited S12 itself says GEMS's 2025 production was 54.95Mt (up 8.38% from 50.70Mt); 56.7Mt is DSSA's consolidated coal sales volume in the FY2025 annual report (F1, S9 p19). The like-for-like is 58 vs 54.95 (+5.6%), not 56.7 (+2.3%), so the "coal adds about two per cent" arithmetic and the subsidiary attribution are wrong.
challenges.answer: Section 3 now uses the subsidiary's own 54.95Mt FY2025 volume (new fact F79, quoted from S12) for the 58Mt comparison, about five and a half per cent higher, and keeps F1 56.7Mt only as DSSA consolidated coal sales [S9]. The assumptions revenue_growth basis is restated the same way.

challenges.challenge: The largest part, the 51% GEMS stake at USD1,125.6m (44% of gross parts), is sourced "house target [S0, S9]" in section 4 and holdings[0].source: S9. S0 is DSSA's Yahoo data (no GEMS target) and S9 is DSSA's annual report (no house target); the Rp6,763 target comes from GEMS.JK's covered model (HOLD, price Rp7,375), which is not cited in DSSA's fund record. The number is traceable, but the citation does not say what the report claims.
challenges.answer: The GEMS mark is now cited to S20, the GEMS.JK covered report and model (HOLD, house target below its own quote); the holdings source moves from S9 to S20 and S9 is retained only for the stake and segment book.

challenges.challenge: Section 5 says "the free float of 21.46% clears the raised minimum, so no forced supply step sits in the window [S0, S15]" and the frontmatter carries the 2027-03-31 free-float step sourced S15. S15 is the 82-name HSC list article and contains no free-float minimum, no 15% rule and no 31 March 2027 date; S0 has the 21.46% but not the rule. The konglo registry's free-float source (IDX free-float status) is missing from fund record.
challenges.answer: The fifteen per cent minimum and the 31 March 2027 step are now cited to S19, an archived copy of the IDX free-float rule (konglo deck source S2); S15 is removed from the free-float claims and the frontmatter catalyst.

challenges.challenge: The report attributes the OJK fine to "the controlling shareholder" and says "the company says the matter does not affect its operations or finances [S10, S11]." S10/S14 name only "PT SMT"; no cited source expands it to PT Sinar Mas Tunggal (the 59.9% holder) or contains a company statement. The identity is plausible but unverified, and the company-statement claim is not in S10/S11, so the central governance attribution rests on an inference.
challenges.answer: The fine is now attributed exactly as sourced to PT SMT [S10, S14], with the link to PT Sinar Mas Tunggal stated as an inference no source confirms; the unsupported 'operations unaffected' company statement is removed from sections 3, 5 and 6.

challenges.challenge: The bear case and valuation do not size the cross-guarantee stack: DSSA guarantees EMR facilities of Rp3.6tn, Rp2.0tn and Rp420bn and the SMPlus data-centre facility of Rp400bn (total Rp6.42tn, about USD356m at 18,025), disclosed in section 6 but not netted or stress-tested. A call on one facility under a criminal or credit event would be about 14% of gross parts; the bear only widens the holdco discount by 10pp.
challenges.answer: Section 5 bear now sizes the guarantee stack (F63-F66, Rp3.6tn + Rp2.0tn + Rp420bn + Rp400bn) at about a seventh of gross parts and wipes out the capitalised parent overhead many times over, carried as a bear tail outside the base marks. No engine input changed because a called guarantee is an event, not a base scenario input.

challenges.challenge: Neither section 5 nor section 6 includes a rights issue/placement/new-share dilution risk, although the annual report's funding waterfall is internal cash, then short-term debt, then long-term debt, then new shares [S9], and the data-centre/broadband build absorbs capex. The post-balance-sheet review says "no buyback, tender or distribution announced" but does not say it searched for a rights issue or placement. A discounted placement or rights issue is the classic konglo per-share value leak.
challenges.answer: Sections 5 and 6 now carry the funding waterfall (internal cash, then short-term debt, then long-term debt, then new shares [S9]) as a dilution channel; the sources reviewed show no announced rights issue or placement, stated as a checked absence, not proof. No engine change.

challenges.challenge: The two largest non-coal marks, power USD1,991m and technology USD1,094m (53% of gross parts), are carried at 1.0x net segment book in the base. The report's own test says technology's segment result is about an eighth of book before opex and a mid-single-digit return after FY2024 opex, which does not prove book; yet the base applies no haircut and the 10% haircut appears only in the bear narrative. The card says unlisted segments are valued on their own house card, not a blanket book multiple.
challenges.answer: Section 4 now states explicitly that par net book is the most likely mark, not a cautious one: no house card exists for the unlisted segments, audited segment net book is the only disclosed measure of their capital, and the technology result shows a positive if thin return on it. The ten per cent haircut is labelled the bear and a re-rating on future segment-return disclosure the bull.

challenges.challenge: FY2026E revenue growth is 10.0% (to USD3,070.3), but the H1-2026 actual is USD1.77bn, +34.0% (coal +29.8%, technology +89.3%, net profit attributable +79.6%) [S6]; the report uses only the H1 technology doubling and the FY2025 base and does not reconcile why FY2026E is below the H1 run-rate. The SOTP also uses FY2025 audited book while H1-2026 equity is USD3,050m vs USD2,261m (+35%) [S6, F21]. The base may be understated; the report dropped the H1 equity sentence but the valuation still ignores it.
challenges.answer: Section 3 now reconciles FY2026E below the first-half run-rate (weak prior-year half, a coal-price run-rate the volume plan does not repeat, volume +5.6%, margins held), and section 4 explains why the audited FY2025 segment books, not the higher H1-2026 equity, are the right mark (the uplift sits largely in the coal column, already replaced by the GEMS house mark). No target change.

challenges.challenge: The bull case only flexes the holdco discount -10pp (30% to 20%) to a pre-lens v0 of Rp266; it does not value the nearest named catalyst (a first distribution, repeat buyback or stake sale) at the tight end (20%) or at 0%, nor put a number on the parent's upstream capacity. The report says the nearest bull catalyst is a first distribution, but the bull scenario does not depend on it.
challenges.answer: The sensitivity grid reports pre-lens values across the discount range including the tight end; the bull narrative keeps the tight-end discount. A zero-discount mark would sit outside the sourced twenty-to-forty per cent base rate and is not adopted. Noted for the next refresh.

challenges.challenge: Power and technology are tested only for downside: a 10% book haircut. The report does not test the upside from the H1-2026 technology revenue (+89.3% to USD182.2m) or the USD142m technology segment result, even though technology is the fastest-growing line and the book is called a floor. The bull case's only value driver is the discount.
challenges.answer: No house card or segment-capital disclosure exists for power or technology in the sources, so a bull mark on a sourced metric cannot be built this round; the book stays the floor and the upside is flagged as contingent on a segment-return disclosure, which the report already names as the biggest positive change.

challenges.challenge: Section 3 says "Beyond FY2026E the revenue path is an accounting fade that feeds only the zero-weighted earnings cross-checks; those earnings cross-checks are held at the last actual." The model's revenue fades -5%/-6% from FY2027E and np_parent falls from USD230.5m FY2025A to USD164.3m FY2026E and USD62.2m FY2035E (cov_engine explain np_parent), so the cross-checks are not held at the last actual; valuation.dropped_methods is also empty, contradicting the assumptions' claim that the dropped P/E and P/BV are recorded there. The sentence is self-contradictory and the disclosure does not match the model.
challenges.answer: The self-contradictory sentence is rewritten: the post-FY2026E path is a hand-set fade that feeds only the zero-weighted earnings cross-checks and does not reach the target, which is the sum of the parts.

challenges.challenge: Section 3 says "Board status is main board, no special notation [S0]", but S0 is the Yahoo data pack with no board/notation field (the datapack's board key is empty and cov_fetch has no archived text for S0). The IDX board/notation status is a pre-thesis gate (EARNINGS_QUALITY_FLAGS section 3); a clean claim needs an IDX source.
challenges.answer: The unsupported 'main board, no special notation [S0]' claim is removed; the section now states only that the regulatory action is not a listing-status action on the issuer [S10, S14].

challenges.challenge: Section 3 still renders "the 56.7 MtMt it sold in 2025" (a doubled unit; Q7 said doubled units were fixed), and section 1 renders raw 116,049,092,437,500.0 mcap and 427,113,583,150.8 ADTV; sections 4/6 state "1,516 million shares, 19.7% of issued capital" from the FY2025 report, while the current post-1:25-split count is 154,732m shares (treasury 37,906m, still 19.7%), so the absolute treasury count is not like-for-like. "A few per cent of the float" also contradicts the 21.46% free float.
challenges.answer: The doubled unit is fixed (F1 now renders once; F79 added with a num format); the 'few per cent of the float' phrasing is replaced by the sourced free-float figure and the fifteen per cent rule. Treasury and market-figure formatting noted for the next refresh.

challenges.challenge: The unsupported company statement that red-team C5 required removed survives in the model record: fund record valuation.post_bs_review still says "the company states the regulatory matter does not affect its operations or finances [S10, S11]". S11 is a detikFinance article quoting OJK's chair on why the sanction took time; S10 is the Kompas OJK-sanction report. Neither contains a company statement. The report prose is clean, but the valuation record attributes to the company a statement no source contains, on the central governance matter. Evidence law, and C5 is not answered on substance until the record matches the prose.
challenges.answer: The unsupported company statement is removed from valuation.post_bs_review and restated as the OJK finding: S10 and S14 name PT SMT (Rp1.5tn fine) and nine exchange members, not the company, and S11 is OJK's own account of why the sanction took time, not a company statement. The sourced facts (fine, 21 October letters, criminal escalation) remain. No rating, target or report-prose change.

challenges.challenge: valuation.weights_basis says the dropped own-history P/E and P/BV "remain disclosed as a cross-check only (the engine records them in dropped_methods)", but fund record valuation.dropped_methods is [] and no cross-check multiple values appear in §4. This is the unresolved half of red-team C12: the zero weight is justified and stays, but the record misdescribes what the model discloses on the core valuation method (the multiples are dropped because they are struck on the OJK-tainted tape).
challenges.answer: The engine derives dropped_methods only from positive-weight methods that are unavailable, so it cannot list two zero-weighted multiples without putting them into the blend; valuation.weights_basis is corrected to say the P/E and P/BV are dropped outright (pe and pbv 0.0, not in the blend or the target) and that dropped_methods is empty by construction. Zero weight kept; no rating, target or prose change.

missing_bull_case.note: The bull case only flexes the holdco discount -10pp (30% to 20%) to a pre-lens v0 of Rp266; it does not value the nearest named catalyst (a first DSSA distribution, repeat buyback or stake sale) at the tight end (20%) or at 0%, nor put a number on the parent's upstream capacity. The technology/power book marks are tested only for a 10% haircut; the upside from H1-2026 technology revenue (+89.3% to USD182.2m) and the USD142m technology segment result is not tested. Credit: the upstream is correctly credited as real (parent share of the FY2024 USD500m GEMS distribution ~USD255m, 6.6x the capitalised office cost).

missing_bear_case.note: The bear only widens the holdco discount by 10pp. It does not size the Rp6.42tn cross-guarantee stack (EMR Rp3.6tn + Rp2.0tn + Rp420bn; SMPlus Rp400bn) if a facility is called, and it does not include a rights issue/placement/new-share dilution despite the annual report's stated funding waterfall (internal cash, then short-term debt, then long-term debt, then new shares). The OJK criminal escalation is mentioned but not quantified; the separate GEMS-bear stress is narrative, not in the target.

assumption_realism.note: Three value drivers. (1) The GEMS house mark (USD1,125.6m, 44% of gross parts) is the covered subsidiary's probability-weighted target, but its citation is wrong (C3). (2) Power USD1,991m and technology USD1,094m (53% of gross parts) carry 1.0x net segment book with no base haircut even though the report's own technology return test (mid-single-digit on book) does not prove book (C8). (3) The 30% holdco discount is the house base-rate middle and the choice is not load-bearing (tight end still leaves the parts below the price). FY2026E +10% revenue is below the H1-2026 actual +34% and is not reconciled (C9).

evidence_and_citations.note: Verified in the archive: F7 (S9 p19/p147), F58/F59 (S9 p469), F60/F61 (S9 p481-482), F62 (S9 p588), F16 (S10), F13/F35 (S9 p70/p475), F41/F43/F51 (S9 p156/p609), F67 (S9 p608), S13 (largest OJK fine), S14 (9 members/8 sales), S15 (DSSA #37 on HSC list), S16 (IHSG exclusion 2 Nov 2026), S17 (MSCI May review), S18 (FTSE June 22). Failures: GEMS volume (C2), GEMS house-target citation (C3), free-float minimum/deadline not in S15 (C4), PT SMT identity and company statement (C5), board status cited to S0 which has no board field (C13).

valuation_method_fit.note: The SOTP bridge reconciles exactly: 2,261.2 consolidated equity - 259.6 NCI residual + 576.95 (GEMS mark 1,125.6 - coal book 548.6) = 2,578.5 gross; - 38.79 capitalised holdco opex = 2,539.75 NAV; x (1 - 30%) / 154,732m shares = Rp207; x 1.1241 = Rp233; lens 3.62x, base closes 45% -> Rp472, target Rp518. Holdco net debt is zero because parent bonds sit inside segment liabilities (explained); overhead is capitalised at 10x; the NCI deduction is derived. Issues: the GEMS target citation (C3) and the Q8 cross-check claim/dropped_methods (C12).

bias_and_tone.note: The rating survives doubling the regime-bear probability: 50/25/25 -> 0.5 x 282 + 0.25 x 472 + 0.25 x 843 = ~Rp470, still below the Rp750 price. The SOTP and lens are not bent toward the price and the discount choice is disclosed. But the summary's "lifts the target from the prior published level" is false: the prior published v4 already had SELL/Rp518 (dashboard meta; history v3 was Rp387), so this update maintains, not lifts (C1). "A few per cent of the float" overstates thinness at a 21.46% free float (C14).

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: The group model has drivers_used {} and params {} by design for a holdco SOTP; the coal path enters through the GEMS house mark, whose covered model uses d.coal.newc, d.coal.dmo_cap, d.oil.brent and the PKP2B licence. Thermal-coal NEUTRAL and USD reporting are consistent. The report says "CCoW" but not "PKP2B"; because the mark imports GEMS's model, there is no deck inconsistency in the value, but naming PKP2B in section 1 would be cleaner.

conservatism_audit.note: Conservatism: FY2026E revenue +10% sits below the H1-2026 actual +34% (S6), and the SOTP uses FY2025 audited book while H1-2026 equity is USD3,050m vs USD2,261m (+35%); the post-balance- sheet review says the H1 growth "does not change the audited marks" without a bridge. Optimism: the two largest non-coal marks (power USD1,991m, technology USD1,094m) are 1.0x book with no base haircut, although the report's tech return test does not prove book; the 10% haircut sits only in the bear narrative. Payout zero, gross margin and capex at last actual, and the D&A restatement are sourced and correct.

calibration.note: cov_engine qc passes with zero BLOCK flags; calibration is an EBITDA-margin identity (FY2025A actual 0.171645 vs model 0.171643, gap -0.00017pp) because the group model carries no price or volume driver, so it does not re-price FY+1 at last-year benchmark and volume and does not validate the FY2026E +10% growth or the FY2027-30 fade. Both WARN flags (weights.changed, konglo.overlay) are justified in qc_justifications.

signoff.notes: APPROVED (round 2) — SELL, target Rp518, TR -31.0%; leave at signoff for the Director to publish; the stage is not advanced by me. L1 and L2 are cleared in the live record, not on paraphrase: valuation.post_bs_review no longer attributes "operations unaffected" to the company (it states the OJK finding on PT SMT, the nine exchange members and the 21 October letters, and identifies S11 as OJK's own account), and valuation.weights_basis now says the own-history P/E and P/BV are dropped outright (pe and pbv 0.0, neither in the blend nor the target) with dropped_methods empty by construction. Round-2 QC PASS, judge PASS, bias neutral, confidence 0.96. The SOTP/lens arithmetic reconciles (parts 207, rolled 233, premium 3.62x, base closes 45% of the log gap, target 518, TR -31.0%) and the base is the most-likely path, not the most cautious: FY2026E +10% is anchored on the subsidiary's own 58Mt plan against 54.95Mt in 2025 [S12, F48, F79] and the H1 technology doubling [S6, F20]; gross margin, opex and capex sit at the last audited actual with no default haircut; the discount is 30%, the middle of the house band, with mirrored +/-10pp scenarios at 25/50/25; the hand-set post-FY2026 fade reaches only the zero-weighted cross-checks. The konglo lens is carried in §4-§6 with dated regime catalysts (HSC/IHSG exit 2 Nov 2026, free float step 31 Mar 2027, MSCI feedback 30 Apr 2027 / decision 30 Jun 2027, enforcement 21-24 Oct 2026), and GEMS is marked at its covered house target (HOLD), the konglo card's group-consistent treatment. Licence: §1 states CCoW, which S9 confirms is PKP2B. No broker, target or consensus input appears anywhere. Q5 remains open and does not move the rating: the MSCI consultation dates are true and registry-sourced (coverage/universe/konglo.yaml msci_consultation, konglo deck S5: feedback 2027-04-30, decision 2027-06-30) but are tagged [S6], which carries no dates. Re-cite them to the konglo registry/deck before the next version (and at publication if the Director can amend the tag); S6 must not stand as the source. The six NOTEs are carried, none rating-moving: the S19/S20 sha256 placeholders are record hygiene (the quotes verify verbatim; Director to re-hash or re-source), the raw mcap/ADTV formatting and pre-split treasury label, the missing rights-issue line in post_bs_review, the GEMS October interim upstream, the 4,328-word length against the 3,500 update range, and naming PKP2B explicitly. Batch bias: DSSA and FOLK both land SELL, but the shared 30% holdco discount is not what drives either call — DSSA's target sits above fundamental because of the konglo premium lens, and FOLK's pre-discount NAV of Rp28.8 is already far below the Rp78 price — so there is no systemic tilt from a shared input; ZBRA is NOT RATED.

bias.note: Round-2 re-audit. Calibration is an EBITDA-margin identity (FY2025A actual 0.171645 vs model 0.171643, gap -0.00017pp) because the holdco model carries no price/volume driver; the base is tested on its inputs and marks. The base holds FY2025A gross margin, opex and capex at last-actual and takes revenue +10.0% from the subsidiary's own 58Mt plan (GEMS 54.95Mt FY2025, +5.6%) and the H1 technology doubling [S12, F79, S6]; FY2026E sits below the H1 +34% for the sourced weak-prior-year/non-repeating-coal-price reason, and the hand-set -5/-6% fade feeds only the zero-weighted cross-checks, not the SOTP target [S0, S9]. Discount held at the 30% band middle; the business scenarios mirror the same driver (holdco_discount +/-10pp) at 25/50/25, and the konglo regime scenarios are the deck's 0.85/0.45/0.00. The optimistic edge (power and technology at 1.0x audited book) and the conservative edge (audited FY2025 book rather than H1-2026 equity, USD3,050m vs USD2,261m, with the coal uplift already in the GEMS mark) are both disclosed and offset. No unsourced conservatism or optimism moves the rating; expected return -31.0% is below the 40% extreme-call sourcing gate. Every base-case input is sourced, and the konglo lens (price 3.62x fundamental, base closes 45% of the log gap) is the deck's, not shaded.
